prompt:
TEXT-ONLY BRIEF (no reference images are attached). Everything in the frame is original to VALLEYWARD.

A finished IN-GAME SCREENSHOT of a real-time browser first-person shooter called VALLEYWARD, 16:9, 1920x1080. This is NOT concept art, NOT a painting, NOT a poster: it is a gameplay frame with the HUD on screen, and it must look achievable in a real-time WebGL browser game.

STYLE (a modern retro first-person horde shooter): first person. The world is chunky blocky 3D: big cube-cut stone blocks, wooden palisade posts, low-poly pine trees; every surface uses LOW-RESOLUTION PIXEL-ART TEXTURES with nearest-neighbour (blocky, unfiltered) texels, like a modern retro shooter: the texels read as small crisp squares on every wall, road, roof and tree (about 16 to 32 texels per metre), with colour variation from block to block and darker joints between the stones. ENEMIES are flat 2D PIXEL-ART SPRITES standing in the 3D world, always facing the camera, about 32x32-pixel sprites drawn big and chunky: small goblins and imps with big heads, pointy ears, ragged tunics, crude spears and torches. Thousands of them. Modern lighting over the retro world: soft volumetric moonlight shafts, fog layers in the valley, bloom, a filmic colour grade, soft vignette.

THE NIGHT: a cold night. Deep teal-indigo sky, a HUGE pale cyan-white full moon low over a misty pine valley, distant blue mountains. Everything that is not fire is cool (teal, indigo, slate blue, grey-green).

THE FIRE (the look of a high-resolution GPU fluid simulation seen up close): fire is a REAL-TIME FLUID SIMULATION spreading over the ground, not particles and not cartoon flame sprites. It curls and swirls into marbled eddies like molten liquid, with a white-yellow core, bright orange body, deep crimson edges, and thick billowing charcoal-brown smoke lit orange from below; thin glowing filaments fold into curls and vortex eddies like glowing ink swirling in water. Fire is the ONLY warm light in the scene: it throws strong orange light onto the nearby stone walls, the ground and the goblin sprites. Burning goblins turn orange-red and run.

COLOUR RULES: warm colours (white-yellow, orange, crimson) belong ONLY to fire, embers and the player's weapon pilot flame. The night, the stone, the forest and the goblins stay cool and muted (olive, ochre-grey, grey-green) unless lit by fire.

HUD (crisp chunky PIXEL FONT, white with a dark outline, small, at the screen edges only): top-centre "NIGHT I  03:12" above a thin wave bar; top-left a thin gold XP bar with "LV 4"; bottom-left a red health bar with "84"; bottom-right "EMBER LANCE" over a small orange fuel gauge. No other text anywhere. No logos, no watermark.

THE PLAYER'S WEAPON (bottom-right of frame, first-person view model): two leather-gloved hands holding the EMBER LANCE, a chunky low-poly flamethrower made of a dented brass fuel tank, iron pipes and a flared iron nozzle with a tiny blue-orange pilot flame; pixel-art textures on it too.

MOMENT M1 "THE ROAD": the player stands on the packed-earth road just outside the open gate of a small stone hill fort and sprays a long stream of fluid fire from the EMBER LANCE down the switchback road. A dense column of hundreds of pixel goblins pours up the road and spills over the grassy slopes toward the camera; thousands more carpet the valley floor below, fading into the moonlit fog. The fire stream hits the column and blooms into a wide curling pool of fluid fire across the road, swirling into marbled eddies, with charcoal smoke rolling uphill; dozens of goblins inside it are burning orange and scattering. Left of frame: the fort's chunky stone wall and an iron brazier. The huge cyan-white moon hangs top-centre-right above the valley. Camera: eye height 1.7 m, looking slightly down the road, FOV about 80 degrees.

FIRE RENDERING STYLE: HYBRID PIXEL FLUID. The fire and smoke keep the same curling, swirling fluid SHAPES, but they are rendered on a coarse pixel grid (each fire pixel about 4 screen pixels wide), with a STEPPED colour ramp of about 6 flat colours (white-yellow, yellow, orange, red-orange, crimson, dark maroon) and ordered dithering where the colours meet and at the smoke edges, so the fire matches the pixel-art world and sprites while still moving like a fluid. The glow and light the fire throws on the world stay smooth.
